reason: E1 states that the strong catalyst-support and electronic effects at the interface endow an electron-deficient state of palladium, which enhances electron transfer and improved activity/durability. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence that this electron-deficient state specifically favors the C1-12e pathway over the C2-4e pathway, nor that the nitrogen dopant concentration is the direct cause of this electronic state. The link between nitrogen content and pathway selectivity is unsupported.
premises: Pd nanoparticles in Pd/Co@N-C are in an electron-deficient state due to interaction with the N-doped graphitic carbon support.
This electron-deficient state enhances electron transfer and catalytic activity/durability for ethanol oxidation.
The N-doped graphitic carbon support is responsible for the electronic interaction that creates the electron-deficient Pd state.
The electron-deficient Pd state favors the complete C1-12e oxidation pathway over the C2-4e pathway.
